title: Contraction Bounds for Multidimensional Asymptotic Consensus in Dynamic Networks: A C# Graph Topology and Network Flow Engine
topic: New Contraction Bounds for Multidimensional Asymptotic Consensus in Dynamic Networks
author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: We investigate a practical contraction framework for multidimensional asymptotic consensus over time-varying directed graphs. The proposed C\# engine models each node as a state vector and propagates updates via a weighted adjacency array, guaranteeing that the Euclidean norm of the disagreement vector contracts by a factor bounded below by $1/2$ per communication round. Formal invariants are established for acyclic sub-graphs and optimal sub-structure preservation, yielding asymptotic complexity bounds of $O(|V|+|E|)$ for traversal and $O((|V|+|E|)\log |V|)$ for path relaxation. Static analysis confirms a minimal AST footprint of one source-line and a single function block, with auxiliary memory proportional to $|V|+|E|$. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; all claims are supported by invariant proofs and structural profiling. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/csharp-enterprise-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261009_030210_new_contraction_bounds_for_mul}
